item.title: Chinese premier to hold '1+10' dialogue with heads of major international economic organizations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 27 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang will hold the "1+10" Dialogue in the city of Xiamen, east China's Fujian Province, on the morning of Dec. 2, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday. According to the spokesperson, Li will hold the dialogue with President of the New Development Bank Dilma Rousseff, President of the World Bank Ajay Banga, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund Kristalina Georgieva, Director-General of the World Trade Organization Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Acting Secretary-General of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development Pedro Manuel Moreno, Assistant Director-General of the International Labour Organization Laura Thompson, Secretary-General of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development Mathias Cormann, General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements Pablo Hernandez de Cos, Chair of the Financial Stability Board Andrew Bailey, and President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Zou Jiayi. The spokesperson said that the theme of the dialogue is "Driving Sustained Growth Through Innovation, Promoting Common Development Through Openness."

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 27 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting, which heard a report on the comprehensive inspection of efforts to promote high-quality development and studied work on further deepening comprehensive investment and financing reforms in the capital market. The meeting also heard a report on the development of the national standards system, and reviewed and approved a draft regulation on the investigation and rectification of potential workplace safety hazards. Solid efforts should be made to rectify problems discovered in the inspection, the meeting said, urging action to ensure that all goals and tasks for the year are accomplished to a high standard. It is imperative to adjust and improve policies and measures that no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development, optimize the incentive and constraint mechanisms, and ensure better coordination of policies, the meeting said. Stressing that the capital market is vital to overall economic development, the meeting called for efforts to strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments and tackle critical reform tasks at the same time. The meeting stressed the need to improve market-stabilizing mechanisms, give full play to existing policies, and mull and introduce new measures to promote steady and sound development of the capital market. According to the meeting, efforts should be made to encourage listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases, give greater play to state-backed funds in steadying the market, and optimize the quasi-"stabilization fund" function of the state-owned Central Huijin Investment Ltd. to provide sufficient liquidity. The meeting also underlined the need to improve policies to support and guide medium- and long-term funds such as insurance funds, enterprise annuities, and social security funds into the market, and strengthen the capacity to guard against and respond to imported risks. It also underlined efforts to boost the internal momentum for high-quality development of the capital market by deepening reform, and to move faster to develop a multi-tiered capital market. It is imperative to strengthen law-based whole-chain supervision and regulation of the capital market, take firm action against financial fraud, non-compliant share reductions and other violations, and effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of investors. The meeting also stressed efforts to systematically improve the standards system, with measures including abolishing local standards that do not meet the requirements of building a unified national market, strengthening the supply of high-quality standards, and taking a forward-looking approach to planning standards for emerging industries and future industries. In terms of workplace safety, the meeting stressed that efforts should focus on key industries and sectors, and that firm measures should be taken to prevent serious and major accidents.

item.title: China unveils roadmap for next-generation communication networks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 -- Chinese authorities have released an implementation plan for the development of next-generation communication networks, aiming to build such networks featuring comprehensive coverage and leading performance by 2030. The plan targets advancing 6G network development at an appropriate time and basically completing the construction of a low-Earth-orbit satellite internet system by 2030. China also expects to promote the large-scale development of integrated networks like the Industrial Internet and the Internet of Vehicles, significantly improve smart development, and further strengthen the industrial ecosystem, according to the plan. It sets out measures to improve basic networks, space-based networks and international networks, as well as integrated networks, while making communication networks smarter, greener, and more secure and resilient. Regarding the industrial ecosystem, the plan calls for accelerating the development of standards for technologies such as 6G, satellite internet and ultra-high-speed optical communications, and the integration of computing resources and communication networks. It also seeks to advance deep-space, deep-Earth, deep-sea and far-sea technological exploration, while promoting the integration of brain-computer interfaces, embodied artificial intelligence and intelligent connected vehicles with next-generation communication networks. The plan encourages private enterprises to participate in network development in accordance with laws and regulations and explore more diverse ways to engage. Stronger support should be given to securing land, forest, grassland, sea and spectrum resources for network development, according to the plan. Next-generation communication networks will form an intelligent, integrated digital infrastructure supported by advanced mobile, fiber-optic and satellite technologies, providing fast, secure and green connectivity. The development of next-generation communication networks is one of six network infrastructure priorities for China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), alongside water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, urban underground pipeline networks and logistics networks. Investment in these six networks and relevant areas is estimated to exceed 7 trillion yuan (about 1.04 trillion U.S. dollars) this year, the National Development and Reform Commission revealed.

item.title: China's police chief meets executive director of UNODC
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- Chinese State Councilor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong met with Monica Juma, executive director of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), in Beijing on Wednesday. Wang said China will resolutely safeguard the core position of the United Nations, deepen practical cooperation with the UNODC in the field of drug control, join hands to address the threat of transnational organized crime, and jointly create a new model of international cooperation in combating telecom fraud. Juma said she highly appreciated China's firm determination and pragmatic achievements in combating transnational crimes such as drugs, and expressed willingness to further strengthen cooperation to jointly address new challenges to global security.

item.title: Chinese vice premier urges joint efforts with Netherlands to keep industrial, supply chains stable
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang on Wednesday called for joint efforts with the Netherlands to ensure that industrial and supply chains remain stable and unobstructed. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when meeting with Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands Tom Berendsen in Beijing. Ding said China and the Netherlands have an open and pragmatic partnership for comprehensive cooperation, and their bilateral cooperation is at the forefront of China-EU cooperation. Noting next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of ambassadorial diplomatic relations between the two countries, Ding said China stands ready to work with the Netherlands to implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, strengthen exchanges and cooperation in all fields, and promote the sound and steady growth of bilateral relations. As major economies in the world, China and the Netherlands should also work together to continuously inject new momentum into the common development of both countries and the world at large, Ding pointed out. Berendsen congratulated China on the successful hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen and spoke highly of China's development achievements. He said the Dutch side stands ready to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, deepen practical cooperation across all fields, properly handle differences through dialogue and consultation, and achieve common development and prosperity.

item.title: Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries. It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission. In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station. Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago. Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity. For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people. He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level.

item.title: Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged continuous and high-quality advancement in the building of regulations and institutions of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and upholding rule-based governance as the basic approach to governing the Party. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on the work related to Party regulations and institutions. Xi said the CPC has made solid efforts and achieved notable achievements in strengthening Party regulations and institutions over the past five years. To provide institutional guarantees for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance and ensuring the Party remains the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, Xi urged enhanced efforts in the systematic integration, education and enforcement of Party institutions, as well as in improving the alignment and coordination of Party rules and regulations with state laws and regulations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on the work related to Party regulations held in Beijing on Tuesday and Wednesday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the meeting. Running the Party through institutions and regulations is one of the core meanings of Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Cai noted, calling for efforts to enhance the level of running the Party through regulations across the board.

item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, Xi said. He said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, combine their respective strengths as major countries in resources, manufacturing and consumption, so as to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go. Xi said that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam.
